title: Form field exit-intent and validation memory patterns
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background: We have multiple pain points surfaced by product analytics and support about form abandonment, repeated validation errors on multi-step flows, and poor behavior when users navigate away and return to a partial form (mobile and desktop). This ticket defines a cohesive set of UX patterns for: exit-intent signaling, validation memory (persisted error/attempt state), and gentle/soft-error affordances that reduce friction without hiding critical failures.

Goals:
- Define deterministic behaviors for when to surface inline errors vs. soft hints vs. blocking error state on field blur, navigation, and submit.
- Specify a small token set and component props that let engineering enable validation-memory and exit-intent heuristics across text fields, selects, toggles, and multi-field compound components.
- Ensure accessibility parity for screen readers (what to announce on return) and keyboard-only flows.
- Provide design specs and microcopy examples for optimistic fixes (auto-format, prefix normalization), autofill reconciliation, and when to keep errors visible after a user leaves the page.

Out of scope: global form persistence across devices (backend sync) and retention policies longer than 24 hours. This ticket focuses on client-side heuristics and component API surface.

Design approach:
1) Exit-intent heuristics: on rapid viewport scroll away, tab close, or focus to a different URL within the app, non-blocking soft hints are promoted to a transient summary toast and inline hints are dimmed after 6s.
2) Validation memory: when enabled, the field component persists last client-side validation result in session storage for that route. On re-entry within 24 hours, fields that previously had soft-errors show a subtle marker (orange bar) and announce "previously flagged" to assistive tech. Blocking errors (server-side or schema failures) remain visible until corrected.
3) Soft-error affordance: soft-errors suggest fixes and are dismissible. They are not included in the form-level blocking validation. Example: "Phone number looks like it's missing country code — try +1..."
4) Autofill and prefill conflict resolution: when browser autofill populates a value that conflicts with our tokenized formatting, prefer canonical display but keep the raw value in the hidden input for submit; display a side hint explaining transformation.

Component API recommendations (spec-level):
- prop: validationMemory: "off" | "session" | "route"
- prop: exitIntentMode: "none" | "soft-toast" | "full-block"
- event hook: onValidationMemoryRestore(previousState)
- token: field-exit-hint-duration = 6000ms
- token: field-memory-visual = "intent-flag-compact"

Acceptance criteria:
- Design spec file (Figma) with annotated variants for TextField, Select, Toggle, and CompoundField showing: normal, soft-error, blocking-error, after-exit, and after-return states.
- Accessibility notes: ARIA live region guidance, announcement strings for restore, and keyboard instructions.
- Microcopy library with 10 canonical soft-error messages and 5 blocking-error templates.
- Component API doc with props and semantics and 2 example usage patterns in Console forms (signup and billing).

Success metrics (for PM/eng to measure post-launch): reduce form abandonment by 8% on flows instrumented, reduce repeated validation failures by 20% within 7 days.

Non-functional constraints: keep DOM changes minimal; prefer CSS-only visual markers where possible; session storage size capped to 5KB per route.

2026-03-04 — Arjun Patel: Ran quick moderated usability tests (n=5) on prototype. Observations: users liked soft hints but were confused when hints disappeared immediately on scroll. Action: increase transient toast duration to 6s and add a persistent subtle marker on the field. Refer: https://figma.com/file/abc123/form-exit-intent

2026-03-06 — Accessibility review (Lina Gomez): Screen reader will need explicit announcement on restore. Proposed announcement string: 'Previous validation noted on [field name] — press enter to review.' Added to ARIA recommendations.

2026-03-09 — Engineering sync (Jamal Rivers): ENG team suggests exposing hook names as onValidationMemoryRestore and onExitIntentDetected. Engineering asks to avoid sessionStorage naming collisions; suggested key prefix 'rw:fm:'. Added to spec.
2026-03-11 — Design review: Finalized token names and amplitude events: form_field_exit_intent, form_field_restore. Shared PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Form+Field+Memory+Patterns
